questions.q: Why did Lesson 29 verify that Conditional Access applied to newly synced users, rather than stopping once the sync itself completed?
options: Zero Trust (Chapter 2) requires continuously verifying sign-ins, so a synced user Conditional Access doesn't evaluate is still a gap
Microsoft Entra Connect automatically disables Conditional Access for new users
Verifying Conditional Access is only necessary for federated, not synced, accounts
Conditional Access is unrelated to hybrid identity sync
questions.explain: Chapter 2's Zero Trust principle treats identity as the perimeter evaluated continuously, so a completed sync that Conditional Access doesn't actually reach is an incomplete fix.

questions.q: What distinguishes the customer-managed key from the database connection string in Lesson 30, even though both live in the same Key Vault?
options: There is no real difference between the two once both are stored in Key Vault
The key can be rotated automatically by Key Vault; the connection string needs a Function to actually rotate its value
The key is Chapter 4's subject and the connection string is Chapter 3's subject
Only the connection string requires purge protection to be enabled
questions.explain: A key's rotation is a cryptographic operation Key Vault can perform itself; a secret's value has to be regenerated by something that understands the target system, such as a Function triggered on near-expiry.

questions.q: What role did Chapter 6's private connectivity play in Lessons 30 and 31, even without its own capstone lab?
options: It was the direct cause of the CSPM finding in Lesson 31
It replaced the need for Conditional Access in Lesson 29
It's the quiet precondition that lets Caldwell's team manage Key Vault and storage over a VPN instead of an open-internet endpoint
It was entirely unused in this chapter's labs
questions.explain: Private connectivity underlies the whole chapter's work by keeping management access off the open internet, even though it isn't the subject of any single capstone lab.

questions.q: According to this review, what was Chapter 7 actually teaching, beyond frameworks like SOC 2 and ISO 27001 in isolation?
options: That SOC 2 only applies to companies without hybrid identity
That compliance frameworks replace the need for encryption and identity controls
That CSPM findings are unrelated to compliance audits
That every other chapter's security work has to be provable to an auditor, not just true
questions.explain: Chapter 7's real lesson is that the technical work from every other chapter has to be demonstrable and auditable, which is why the CMK and the re-scanned CSPM fix both matter on a compliance report.

questions.q: Which course comes next in the Cloud Engineer to Cloud Architect path after this course completes?
options: Docker & Kubernetes Container Platforms
PowerShell, Python, Azure CLI & Infrastructure Automation
Enterprise Cloud Architecture Capstone
Terraform IaC for Cloud Architects
questions.explain: This course closes the identity/networking/security segment of the Job-Ready Foundation stage, and the path continues into scripting and infrastructure automation next.
